head: claude/phase-f-c3-decision-prep
title: Phase F/C3: the committed decision record gets a reader, and says what it could not grade
body:
## ⚠️ First: my brief was stale, and this PR corrects it rather than acting on it

I was pointed at the build plan's Phase F finding — *"`strategy_review_packet.py` … writes to a **gitignored path with no cron**. The repair is a cron and a committed path."* **RULE ONE: I verified instead of taking the doc's word, and two of the three parts already shipped today.**

| Part | State | Evidence I checked myself |
|---|---|---|
| A schedule that runs it | ✅ **already shipped** | `.github/workflows/strategy-review-packets.yml` — `cron: "40 4 * * *"` + `workflow_dispatch` + issue-driven |
| A committed path | ✅ **already shipped** | `comms/strategy_reviews/2026-09-01/` on `main` — `INDEX.json` `graded=52 · actionable=0 · by_action={"hold": 52}` |
| A reader | ❌ **missing — this PR** | grep-verified below |

Landed by **#10649** (merged 11:58Z today), repaired by **#10653**. Building either again would be `RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED`, whose cheap preventer is exactly the existence check that produced this table. **The Phase F paragraph is corrected in this PR** — left as written it invites the next session to rebuild a shipped mechanism, which is stale in the expensive direction.

## The gap that was real

`grep` over `*.py`/`*.ts`/`*.svelte`/`*.yml` for `comms/strategy_reviews` returns **the writer and the docs and nothing else**. The committed decision record had **zero consumers**. The only route, `GET /api/bot/strategies/{name}/review`, reads `runtime_logs/strategy_reviews/` — `.gitignore:29`, VM-local, gone on re-provision — and is **per-strategy only**, so *"what did the fleet grade today and what does it propose"* could not be asked without opening 52 files.

A record written and never read is what `provenance-consumer-guard` exists to catch. Here it is the C3 failure one level up: the packet becomes durable and still reaches no decision.

**`GET /api/bot/strategy-reviews`** closes it — the day's `INDEX` (the denominator: every strategy graded, including every HOLD), the proposed actions, per-row `packet_committed`, and history. Built on `reports.py`'s shape, the precedent the plan itself names.

## 🔴 The part that matters more than the route

**`actionable: 0` is two different facts and they rendered identically:** *the fleet is fine*, and *nothing could be graded*.

**Population — all 52 enabled strategies, the committed 2026-09-01 index, window 7 days:**

| `n_closed` | strategies |
|---|---|
| 0 | **34** |
| 1–4 | 14 |
| 5–19 | 4 |
| **20+** | **0** |

The generator forces HOLD below `MIN_CLOSED_FOR_ACTION = 20` (the PB-20260630-004 floor, which is **correct** — a real-money KILL off 1–5 trades is noise). So **52/52 sat under the floor and no leg could produce a KILL/DEMOTE whatever its PnL** — including **13 losing legs** carrying **−$35,446** of *provenance-trusted* PnL between them (the packet already excludes rows whose provenance is not measured/estimated, so this is not a fabricated-mark figure).

**The arithmetic makes it permanent:** at a 7-day window a leg needs ~3 closes/day to be gradeable, against a fleet-wide **50 closes that week**. The floor is unreachable for every leg, every run, indefinitely.

**Neither component is wrong on its own** — the floor is deliberate and defended, the window is a reasonable default, and each was chosen without reference to the other. The defect lives at the seam, which is why it survived review.

So this PR makes the condition **visible**: the generator publishes `min_closed_for_action` + per-row `below_evidence_floor`, and the route reports an `evidence` block with `floor_state`. **Derived from the generator's published NUMBER, never by matching the English in `reasons`** — that is sub-class **A** of the diagnostic-provenance defect, the exact reasoning that defers C4, and I am not routing around it.

## ❓ THE DECISION I AM NOT TAKING — needs an operator

**Widening `WINDOW_DAYS` would make the fleet gradeable. I did not do it.** It is not in my forbidden set (it is a workflow env var, not `strategies.yaml`/risk caps/an order path) but it **changes what evidence a KILL badge rests on**, and a KILL widened far enough to make anything gradeable is the same low-n hazard the floor exists to prevent, one level up.

**The question for the operator: what evidence should a KILL/DEMOTE badge rest on?** Window and floor are only meaningful together — pick the pair, not one side. Filed as `BL-20260901-REVIEW-PACKET-WINDOW-AND-EVIDENCE-FLOOR-ARE-INCOMPATIBLE-SO-NO-ACTION-CAN-EVER-FIRE` (**high**).

## How a produced packet actually reaches a decision — asked and answered honestly

My brief demanded evidence on this. **Today it does not.** The chain is evidence → packet → **decision**, and the packet end is now durable, reachable and self-describing, while the decision end is still empty for the structural reason above. Two links remain, both filed rather than claimed as done:

1. **Nothing renders it.** A route is not a reader — the SPA and Streamlit both show the per-strategy card and neither knows the fleet index exists. I have moved the written-and-never-read defect one hop, not eliminated it, and say so plainly. `BL-20260901-COMMITTED-REVIEW-RECORD-HAS-A-ROUTE-BUT-STILL-NO-RENDERED-CONSUMER` (**medium**) — with the instruction that any panel must render `evidence.floor_state` and `freshness` **beside** the action count, or it reintroduces the very error this block exists to end.
2. **The packet proposes nothing** (above).

## ⚠️ The cron is DEPLOYED, NOT OBSERVED

It landed **11:58Z** today and fires at **04:40 UTC**, so **its first scheduled opportunity has not arrived**. That is a third state, distinct from *fired and worked* and *fired and failed*, and I will not let it read as either. Both runs to date (#10652, #10656) were dispatch-driven. `OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON` is a live counter-example in this repo, so correct cron syntax is **not** evidence of firing.

I could not check run history: `api.github.com` returns **403** in this sandbox (as `CLAUDE.md` documents) and no Actions MCP tool is in this session's toolset. Stating that as a limit rather than inferring a clean negative.

## Collapsed states — two new contracts registered

Both registered with `collapsed-state-guard` (**22 contracts, clean**):

- **`read_state`** `index_read`/`absent`/`unreadable` — a corrupt index must never render as an empty fleet. That is sub-class **C** and the consumer side of `silent-empty-guard`, and it matters more here than on a soak surface: this record is read *before* a Tier-3 decision, where *"nothing needs attention"* and *"we could not tell"* are opposite inputs.
- **`freshness`** `fresh`/`stale`/`undateable`/`absent` — the defect `/api/bot/prop/status` grew `status_freshness` for. `undateable` **fails safe to not-fresh**: a record that cannot be *dated* cannot be shown *current*.

Counts are **`null`, never `0`**, when we could not look — 0 graded is a real reading. The **denominator survives** `actionable_only`.

⚠️ **Coverage caveat, stated not papered over:** the route is new, so both contracts' state coverage is satisfied by **tests**, not a production consumer. Registered anyway — the states exist and the guard's job is to stop a later change quietly folding them together. Recorded in each contract's `why`, following `ib_venue_session`'s precedent.

While registering, a first-cut `\bfreshness\b` consumer token **fired on three unrelated files** (`standard_account_size.py`, `manager_lease.py`, `test_news_layer.py`) that merely share the word. Narrowed — coincidence-firing is what produces a routinely-overridden alarm.

## Verification

- **106 tests pass** across the strategy-review suites; **23 new**, including a **generator→route round-trip** so producer and consumer cannot drift on the floor (re-deriving a generator-owned rule is what produced the 105-file PR).
- `collapsed-state-guard` **clean (22 contracts)** · `api-tier-policy` **OK** (the route carries its row) · `diagnostic-provenance` **OK** · `backlog round-trip` **OK, 3 backlogs byte-for-byte** (the append is **+27/−0** — no reattribution).
- The route was exercised against the **real committed record**, not only fixtures: `read_state=index_read`, `graded=52`, `actionable=0`, `freshness=fresh`, and `evidence.floor_state=unknown` — correctly `unknown`, because that index predates the published field and guessing would assert an observation nobody made.

⚠️ **Not verified:** neither route has been observed serving from the live VM; they are exercised against the committed store in-process. And `pytest`/`lint-imports` absences in this sandbox are tooling, not defects — I installed pytest locally to run the suites above.

## Tier + scope

**Tier-1 throughout** — read path, docs, and a guard registration. **No `config/strategies.yaml`, no risk caps, no order path.** **C4 not taken** — deferred with a reason I am not routing around.

Also filed: `BL-20260901-COMMITTED-REVIEW-DAY-HOLDS-105-FILES-FROM-THE-PRE-FIX-SELECTOR` (**low**) — the one committed day carries all 52 packets though its index says `actionable: 0`, a known-and-fixed selector case-mismatch, left rather than swept because deleting history to match a contract it predates is the wrong instinct.

Draft pending CI.
